exercises.title: Unpin with a check
analysisLines: Qf1+ Qf5 Bxa5 Bd4+ Kh2 Qxf1

content.prompt: White to move. White would like to capture the knight on a5, but the bishop on c3 is pinned. How should White solve this problem?
content.hint: The bishop is pinned because your queen stands behind it. Can the queen leave that diagonal with gain of time?
content.explanation: Qf1+ takes the queen out of the pin with check. After Qf5 White must not hurry: Bxa5 would lose the queen to Bd4+, so first Qxf5+ gxf5 and only then Bxa5. The direct Bxe5 dxe5 Qxe5 Nc6 just leaves Black a pawn up. Book continuation: Qf1+ Qf5 Qxf5+ gxf5 Bxa5 (or Qf1+ Kg8 Bxa5).

exercises.title: Win a piece along the way

content.prompt: White to move. Black is offering to trade queens. How can White win a piece along the way?
content.hint: The bishop on e7 is protected by nothing. Can you attack it and the queen with one move?
content.explanation: Nd5 attacks the queen and the bishop on e7. After Qxb3 White does not recapture at once: the intermediate check Nxe7+ wins the bishop first, and then axb3 takes the queen. Book continuation: Nd5 Qxb3 Nxe7+ Kh8 axb3.

content.prompt: White to move. How can White gain a material advantage?
content.hint: Two rooks attack each other on the c-file. What can your other rook take, and how does it get out of danger?
content.explanation: Rxd6 wins the knight. If Black takes on c3, the rook on d6 escapes with the intermediate check Rd8+ and then bxc3 recaptures, so White stays a piece ahead. Book continuation: Rxd6 Rxc3 Rd8+ Kg7 bxc3.

content.prompt: White to move. White can win the exchange. Can you see how?
content.hint: The queens look at each other through your knight. Where can the knight go with an attack of its own?
content.explanation: Ng4 attacks the rook on f6 and uncovers the queen on g3 against the queen on c7. After Qxg3 the intermediate check Nxf6+ wins the rook before hxg3. Protecting the queen with Rc6 does not help because of Nf6+, when the g-pawn is pinned. Book continuation: Ng4 Qxg3 Nxf6+ gxf6 hxg3 (or Ng4 Rc6 Nf6+).

content.prompt: White to move. Both bishops point toward the black king, but the immediate Bxf6 has a problem. How can White fix it?
content.hint: Bxf6 at once runs into a mate on your back rank. Which black piece gives that mate, and can you push it away with gain of time?
content.explanation: The immediate Bxf6 allows Qxe1 mate. So White first plays Bc3, attacking the queen and covering e1. After Qb6 the capture Bxf6 works: gxf6 allows Qxh7 mate, and after g6 White plays Qh6 with mate on g7 to follow. Book continuation: Bc3 Qb6 Bxf6 gxf6 Qxh7# (or Bc3 Qb6 Bxf6 g6 Qh6).

exercises.title: The unprotected queen
bookLines: Rxb5 Qxa3 Rb7+ Rf7 Rxf7+ Kxf7 bxa3

content.prompt: White to move. The black queen stands on an unprotected square. How can White take advantage of that?
content.solutionText: Rxb5 Qxa3 Rb7+ Rf7 Rxf7+ Kxf7 bxa3
content.hint: Your rook defends your queen, and the black queen is protected by nothing. What can the rook take?
content.explanation: Rxb5 wins the bishop, because cxb5 loses the queen on e7. After Qxa3 White inserts the check Rb7+, trades rooks on f7, and only then recaptures the queen with bxa3. Book continuation: Rxb5 Qxa3 Rb7+ Rf7 Rxf7+ Kxf7 bxa3.

content.prompt: White to move. Black is offering to trade knights, but White can gain a serious material advantage. What is the right move?
content.hint: The black queen and king stand on the same diagonal. What happens to the knight on e7 if the queen has to leave e6?
content.explanation: Qb3 pins the queen against the king. After Qxb3 White takes the knight with check, Nxe7+, and then recaptures the queen with cxb3, coming out a knight ahead. Book continuation: Qb3 Qxb3 Nxe7+ Kh8 cxb3.

content.prompt: White to move. How can White gain a serious material advantage?
content.hint: The black queen has to protect the rook on b8. Can you force it to give up that job?
content.explanation: Qd4 offers a trade that Black cannot accept safely. After Qxd4 White first takes the rook with check, Rxb8+, and then the queen with exd4. Protecting the queen with f6 loses the rook in the same way after Qxe5. Book continuation: Qd4 Qxd4 Rxb8+ Kg7 exd4 (or Qd4 f6 Qxe5 fxe5 Rxb8+).

content.prompt: White to move. Black has just attacked the white queen, yet White has a winning combination. What is the right continuation?
content.hint: Your queen is attacked, but the rook on e8 is protected only by the black queen. Can you pull that queen away with check?
content.explanation: Qf4+ forces the black queen to take on f4. Now the rook on e8 has lost its protection: Rxe8+ is an intermediate check, and then gxf4 recaptures the queen. Book continuation: Qf4+ Qxf4 Rxe8+ Kc7 gxf4.

content.prompt: White to move. Black has an extra knight. How can White win it back?
content.hint: The black queen and king stand on the same long diagonal, and the knight on h5 is pinned on the h-file.
content.explanation: Qc3 pins the queen against the king. After Qxc3 White takes the knight with check, Rxh5+, and then recaptures the queen with Nxc3. After f6 the same idea works: Qxe5 fxe5 Rxh5+. Book continuation: Qc3 Qxc3 Rxh5+ Kg7 Nxc3 (or Qc3 f6 Qxe5 fxe5 Rxh5+).

content.prompt: Black to move. The bishop is pinned, and after Bxc3 Black would lose the rook on e3. How can Black improve the position of the rook first?
content.hint: The rook on e3 would be lost after Bxc3 because the bishop no longer protects it. Where can the rook go with check so that the bishop protects it afterwards?
content.explanation: Re1+ moves the rook with check to a square that the bishop will protect from c3. After Kc2 Bxc3 the white rook can only trade on e1, and Black has won a piece. Book continuation: Re1+ Kc2 Bxc3.

content.prompt: White to move. Again the black queen stands on an unprotected square. What should White play?
content.hint: The queens look at each other through your knight. Which knight move attacks something that is not protected?
content.explanation: Ne4 uncovers the queen on e1 against the queen on a5 and attacks the unprotected knight on f6. After Qxe1 the intermediate check Nxf6+ wins the knight before Rfxe1, and after Nxe4 White simply takes the queen. Book continuation: Ne4 Qxe1 Nxf6+ Kh8 Rfxe1 (or Ne4 Nxe4 Qxa5).

exercises.title: The right way to make luft
bookLines: f3 Ne3 Rxb7 Rc1+ Kf2 Nd1+ Ke2

content.prompt: White to move. White has a back-rank problem. What should White do to fix it?
content.solutionText: f3 Ne3 Rxb7 Rc1+ Kf2 Nd1+ Ke2
content.hint: You want to take the bishop on b7, but first the king needs a flight square. Choose the pawn move that leaves Black no intermediate move.
content.explanation: Rxb7 at once is forbidden because of Rc1+. The move f3 makes room for the king and attacks the knight, and after Ne3 Rxb7 Black has only a couple of checks: Rc1+ Kf2 Nd1+ Ke2. The other pawn move, h3, is weaker: Black has the intermediate move Be4, and after Re1 Nf6 everything is protected. Book continuation: f3 Ne3 Rxb7 Rc1+ Kf2 Nd1+ Ke2.

content.prompt: White to move. How can White win material?
content.hint: The queens look at each other through your knight. Two knight moves attack the rook on f6; which one attacks a second rook as well?
content.explanation: Nd7 uncovers the queen on g3 and attacks both rooks. After Qxg3 Nxf6+ gxf6 hxg3 White has won the exchange; after Rc6 Qxc7 Rxc7 Nxb8 or Qxd7 Qxb8+ White wins a rook. Ng4 is not as good, because Black can answer Rc6. Book continuation: Nd7 Qxg3 Nxf6+ gxf6 hxg3 (or Nd7 Rc6 Qxc7 Rxc7 Nxb8) (or Nd7 Qxd7 Qxb8+).

content.prompt: White to move. The black queen is pinned. How can White use the pin to gain material?
content.hint: The pinned queen is protected by the rook on d8. Which of your pieces can attack the queen once more?
content.explanation: Rd1 attacks the pinned queen. After Qxb3 White takes the rook with check, Rxd8+, and only then recaptures the queen with axb3. Book continuation: Rd1 Qxb3 Rxd8+ Kf7 axb3.

content.prompt: White to move. How can White take advantage of the unfortunate position of the black pieces?
content.hint: The black queen is the only protector of the rook on a8. How can you force it to leave?
content.explanation: Qc4 offers a queen trade. After Qxc4 the rook on a8 has lost its protection: Rxa8+ is an intermediate check, and then bxc4 recaptures the queen. Book continuation: Qc4 Qxc4 Rxa8+ Kh7 bxc4.

content.prompt: White to move. White seems to have two ways to reach the same goal, but only one of them works. Which one?
content.hint: A rook move uncovers your queen against the black queen. Which square also ties down the rook on d8?
content.explanation: Rc8 uncovers the queen on e3 against the queen on b6 and pins the rook on d8. After Qxe3 White takes the rook with check, Rxd8+, and then recaptures with fxe3. The other try, Rd5, fails to Qb8, when everything is protected. Book continuation: Rc8 Qxe3 Rxd8+ Kh7 fxe3.

content.prompt: White to move. Black has just captured a rook on e1. The obvious reply is Kxe1. Does White have a better option?
content.hint: The rook on e1 will not run away. Your bishop looks at the black king through the bishop on f5; which piece should capture there?
content.explanation: Rxf5 wins a piece and threatens a discovered check, so Black has no time to save the rook on e1: after Kg7 or Rxf5 Bxf5+ White takes it next move, and after Rfe8 the discovered check Re5+ wins it as well. The obvious Kxe1 allows Re8+, and Bxf5+ Rxf5 Rxf5 Re7 does not do much for White either. Book continuation: Rxf5 Kg7 Kxe1 (or Rxf5 Rxf5 Bxf5+ Kg7 Kxe1) (or Rxf5 Rfe8 Re5+ Kg7 Rxe1).

exercises.title: Take the knight
bookLines: Rxd7 Qxc1 Rd8+ Re8 Rxe8+ Bxe8 Nxc1

content.prompt: White to move. How can White win a piece?
content.solutionText: Rxd7 Qxc1 Rd8+ Re8 Rxe8+ Bxe8 Nxc1
content.hint: Your rook is pinned against the queen. What can it capture, and how does it get away after the queens come off?
content.explanation: Rxd7 takes the knight and uncovers the queen on c1 against the queen on g5. After Qxc1 White does not recapture at once: the intermediate check Rd8+ saves the rook, and after Re8 Rxe8+ Bxe8 Nxc1 White is a piece ahead. Book continuation: Rxd7 Qxc1 Rd8+ Re8 Rxe8+ Bxe8 Nxc1.

exercises.title: Something even better
analysisLines: Rxb3 Be5+ Kf7 fxe4 Bxe4 d6

content.prompt: Black to move. White has just captured a knight with Bxd6. Black can choose which bishop to capture, or look for something even better.
content.hint: If you take one bishop, the other one escapes with check. Is there a move that changes that?
content.explanation: After Rxb3 White saves the other bishop with Be5+ and has no problems. Instead e3+ forks the king and the rook, so White has to take: Kxe3. Now Rxb3 comes with check, and after Ke2 Black takes the second bishop with exd6. Book continuation: e3+ Kxe3 Rxb3+ Ke2 exd6.

content.prompt: White to move. Black has just played axb4. Show why this was a mistake.
content.hint: The a-file has just been opened in front of your rook. Which black piece now protects the rook on a8, and can you pull the queen onto an attacked square first?
content.explanation: Bxc5 Qxc5 brings the queen to c5. Then axb4 attacks the queen and uncovers the rook on a1 against the rook on a8: after Qxc4 White takes on a8 and has won a rook. (The book's diagram shows the position before Black's move axb4.) Book continuation: Bxc5 Qxc5 axb4 Qxc4 Rxa8.

content.prompt: White to move. All four rooks are hanging. How can White come out of this mess ahead?
content.hint: All four rooks are attacked. Before capturing anything, look for a check that disturbs the black defenders.
content.explanation: Bc6+ comes first. If the king takes, Rh6+ saves the attacked rook with check and then Rxf7 wins the exchange. If the knight takes, Rxf7+ comes with check and Rxc8 follows. If the rook takes, it no longer attacks the rook on h8 and White simply plays Rxf7. Book continuation: Bc6+ Kxc6 Rh6+ Kd7 Rxf7 (or Bc6+ Nxc6 Rxf7+ Ke6 Rxc8) (or Bc6+ Rxc6 Rxf7).

exercises.title: Better than recapturing the queen
bookLines: Nxe1 Kf1 Nf3+ Ke2 Nd4+ Kd3 Nxf5

content.prompt: Black to move. White has just captured the black queen. Does Black have anything better than recapturing with gxf5?
content.hint: The white queen will still be attacked next move. Your rook pins the knight on e1 against the king; what can you do with that?
content.explanation: Nxe1 wins a piece and threatens a discovered checkmate. If White saves the queen with Qxf7, Nf3 is mate by double check. If the king runs, Kf1 Nf3+ Ke2 Nd4+ Kd3 Nxf5 wins the queen anyway. Book continuation: Nxe1 Qxf7 Nf3# (or Nxe1 Kf1 Nf3+ Ke2 Nd4+ Kd3 Nxf5).

exercises.title: Go for the king
bookLines: Qg5 Qg6 Qxh5+ Kg8 Bxg6 fxg6 Qxg6+ Kh8 Qg7#

content.prompt: White to move. White can capture the black queen, but Black would still be ahead in material. How can White win the game quickly?
content.solutionText: Qg5 Qg6 Qxh5+ Kg8 Bxg6 fxg6 Qxg6+
content.hint: The black queen is pinned and cannot run away. What does your queen threaten if it comes closer to the king instead?
content.explanation: The pinned queen will not run away, so White goes for the king: Qg5 threatens mate on g7. After Qg6 Qxh5+ Kg8 White takes the queen under better conditions, Bxg6 fxg6 Qxg6+ Kh8, and Qg7 is checkmate. Book continuation: Qg5 Qg6 Qxh5+ Kg8 Bxg6 fxg6 Qxg6+ Kh8 Qg7#.

exercises.title: No need to move the queen
bookLines: fxg2 Nxc7 Nf4 Qb3 Ngxh3+ Qxh3+ Bxh3

content.prompt: Black to move. White has just played Nc3-b5, attacking the queen. How should Black react?
content.solutionText: fxg2 Nxc7 Nf4 Qb3 Ngxh3+ Qxh3+ Bxh3
content.hint: Your queen is attacked, but look at the white king first. What do your pawn on f3 and your two knights threaten?
content.explanation: There is no need to move the queen. After fxg2 Nxc7 Nf4 Black threatens mate on h3, and Qb3 Ngxh3+ Qxh3+ Bxh3 leaves White helpless against Ne2 mate. If White takes the pawn with Kxg2, the queen simply moves away with Qd7 and Black has won a piece. Book continuation: fxg2 Nxc7 Nf4 Qb3 Ngxh3+ Qxh3+ Bxh3 (or fxg2 Kxg2 Qd7).
